sources.entry: Highway - Defines sizeless vector types with run-time dispatch, so one source serves SVE and every fixed-width ISA.

summary.one_liner: Highway is a C++ library of portable SIMD/vector intrinsics that lets one codebase target many CPU instruction sets, selecting the best available one at compile time or run time.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a set of SIMD/vector operations (load, store, arithmetic, masks, comparisons, gather/scatter, and more) that map to CPU instructions. Application code is written once and can be built for static dispatch to a single instruction set or dynamic dispatch that picks the best supported target at runtime, switched by changing HWY_STATIC_DISPATCH to HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH. It supports scalable vectors (size unknown at compile time) as well as fixed-width ISAs, using tags such as ScalableTag and FixedTag. The README describes strip-mining strategies for handling loop remainders, plus a built-in profiler and examples in hwy/examples. Build uses CMake, with Bazel also supported.
use_cases: portable SIMD code across x86, Arm, RISC-V, POWER and WebAssembly
runtime CPU feature dispatch in a C++ application
vectorized sorting, compression and linear algebra
replacing hand-written intrinsics with a portable API
benchmarking SIMD loops against scalar code
notable: Supports 27 targets across x86 (SSE2 through AVX10_2), Arm NEON/SVE/SVE2, RISC-V RVV, POWER, IBM Z, LoongArch and WebAssembly
Same application code works with static or dynamic dispatch, with a one-line switch between them
Scalable-vector support (SVE, RVV) alongside fixed-width ISAs
Ships design docs: quick_reference.md, instruction_matrix.md, faq.md
Dual-licensed Apache 2 / BSD-3 per the README
caveats: Ops must be called inside HWY namespace or with aliases, and functions need HWY_ATTR or the namespace macros, which adds some boilerplate
Armv7 builds need the -DHWY_CMAKE_ARM7 CMake flag, and 32-bit x86 is not officially supported
Compiler flags must match baseline targets for static dispatch, and optimizations (-O2) are needed for good performance
